jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Workforce Insight Solutions Leader is accountable for the full lifecycle of the Workforce Insight product portfolio, from identified need through build on Helix to measured adoption by leaders across all functions and regions. The role is the single global owner of workforce insight products for Equinix. The portfolio includes cross-domain leadership products that combine People data with business data. The role leads the insight consulting relationship with TPT Functions, runs the Insight Solutions delivery engine (intake, requirements, portfolio, roadmap and standards) and owns the product build and people-domain data strategy in direct partnership with DIO. It sets the AI analytics strategy for the portfolio, which is how insight products progress from descriptive reporting towards assisted, conversational and agentic insight, and is accountable to People leadership for the portfolio’s contribution to the Future Ready Team’s outcomes.

Responsibilities

Product & Portfolio Strategy

Own the Workforce Insight product portfolio: set the roadmap, prioritisation logic and sunset decisions, anchored to measurable use, impact and outcomes
Define and execute the AI analytics strategy for the portfolio, including the view on how insight products move from dashboards to AI-assisted, conversational and agentic delivery, and the sequence to get there
Define and enforce the WFI product standard (definitions, design patterns, access model, release discipline) so that every product in the portfolio is recognisably one family
Own the productisation path for Workforce Decision Intelligence and Equinix Brain outputs
Make build, buy or partner decisions on tooling and platforms for the insight product stack, in concert with People Tech Ops and EDNA teams
Manage the capacity plan, tooling budget and contingent and vendor resources for the engine, including the people-domain engineering capacity shared with DIO

Insight Partnering (TPT Functions)

Lead the team of TPT Insight Partners in working with senior HR leaders to identify their workforce insight needs, assess those needs against existing products and execute a plan to close the gaps
Shape demand into a coherent portfolio
Own measurement design for People programmes
Lead the development and delivery of cross-domain workforce insight products
Partner with WFI and People Strategy leaders and FPT Insight Partners to shape the portfolio

Product Build & Data Foundations

Lead the DevOps capability that builds insight products on Helix
Act as business owner of the people-domain data strategy and Helix ingestion roadmap
Own People data quality and governance standards for insight products
Represent Workforce Insights as the accountable partner to DIO, People Tech Ops and EDNA

Adoption & Feedback Loop

Design and run a continuous feedback and prioritisation loop
Embed agile and design-thinking practice across the engine
Own product marketing and enablement for the portfolio
Accountable to the People Leadership Team for portfolio health

Team Leadership

Lead and develop a globally distributed, multi-disciplinary team plus contingent and vendor resources
Build a diverse, inclusive, product-minded team culture and coach the wider WFI team

Qualifications

Knowledge and Experience

Significant experience in analytics, people analytics or data products, including leading teams
Proven ownership of a product portfolio at enterprise scale
Track record as a trusted consultant to senior HR or business leaders
Experience directing a build team on a modern cloud data platform
Applied experience bringing GenAI and LLM capability into analytics products
Working knowledge of data governance, data quality and access models for sensitive people data
Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative or relevant discipline; Master’s preferred

Skills & Attributes

Product leadership, with discovery, design thinking, agile delivery and outcome measurement as established working practice
Business and financial acumen
Technically credible with engineers and data platform leaders without needing to build personally
Strong stakeholder leadership across HR, IT and enterprise data functions
Clear, concise communicator of complex data-driven insight to senior HR and business leaders
Comfortable operating at portfolio level under ambiguity and able to establish an operating rhythm where none exists

jobs.title: Director, Portfolio Management
jobs.description:
WHY JOIN US?

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week
. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.

About AISI

AstraZeneca AI for Science Innovation (AISI) is driving the convergence of artificial intelligence and life sciences at enterprise scale. AISI brings together data foundations, AI and machine-learning technology, strategic partnerships, process reinvention, and business-facing AI to accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery. Success depends on connecting and scaling existing capabilities, promoting reuse, and translating innovation into measurable scientific, patient, and enterprise value.

The Opportunity

The Director, Portfolio Management will lead the design, governance, and continuous improvement of AISI's portfolio management capability across strategic initiatives, AI and data platforms, external partnerships, projects, suppliers, managed services, and operational investments. The role ensures that strategy is translated into an executable portfolio, investments and resources are directed to the highest-value opportunities, delivery performance is transparent, and financial and operational risk, and compliance governance are embedded throughout the portfolio lifecycle.

Operating at the intersection of AISI leadership, scientific and therapeutic-area stakeholders, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, HR, and external partners, the Director will establish scalable ways of working, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, and deliver outcomes through cross-functional teams and managed-service providers. The role sits within AISI Operations and reports to the Head of AISI Operations.

Scope And Core Accountabilities

Portfolio Strategy, Planning, and Governance

Translate AISI strategy and scientific priorities into an integrated portfolio of investments, initiatives, platforms, products, partnerships, and operational services.
Establish and continuously improve demand intake, assessment, value-based prioritization, funding, resource allocation, stage-gate review, delivery assurance, and benefits-realization processes.
Maintain an integrated portfolio view, identifying opportunities to stop, sequence, accelerate, consolidate, reuse, or scale initiatives as priorities and evidence evolve.
Lead portfolio governance forums and provide clear executive reporting on investment, demand, delivery health, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, capacity, financial performance, and expected value.
Develop standardized dashboards and management information that enable timely, transparent, evidence-based decisions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Financial and Investment Management

Partner with Finance and senior leaders to manage long-term investment planning, business cases, budgets, forecasts, and Run and Change expenditure.
Oversee forecast-versus-budget analysis, variance management, accruals, cross-charges, resource recharges, purchase orders, and supplier-related financial commitments.
Ensure financial information is accurate, timely, transparent, and connected to portfolio priorities, delivery milestones, and benefits realization.
Define and track financial and non-financial value measures, including scientific impact, speed, adoption, reuse, risk reduction, productivity, and enterprise scalability.

Operating Model and Process Excellence

Design and evolve the portfolio operating model, decision rights, governance forums, escalation pathways, and RACI frameworks required to manage a complex, global portfolio.
Drive standardization, simplification, automation, and continuous improvement across portfolio, project, financial, supplier, contracting, resource, onboarding, and service-management processes.
Introduce fit-for-purpose Agile, Lean Portfolio Management, Design Thinking, incremental delivery, and hybrid governance practices where appropriate.
Ensure processes are practical, adopted, and supported by reliable data and fit-for-purpose tools, including ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and portfolio or financial-management platforms.

Partnership, Contracting, and Supplier Governance

Provide end-to-end portfolio oversight of strategic alliances, AI and data partnerships, technology providers, suppliers, and managed services.
Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, Privacy, Information Security, and technical leaders across the contracting lifecycle, from intake, due diligence, term-sheet development, and negotiation through execution, performance review, renewal, and exit.
Implement supplier and partner governance through scorecards, service-level agreements, periodic business reviews, delivery-quality measures, commercial-health monitoring, risk mitigation, and value-for-money assessments.
Ensure partner commitments, dependencies, milestones, financial obligations, and benefits are integrated into portfolio planning and reporting.

Resource and Capacity Management

Lead resource and capacity-management practices across projects, products, platforms, partnerships, and operational services.
Oversee workforce planning, allocation, utilization, people recharges, onboarding, and prioritization of scarce scientific, AI, engineering, and portfolio-management capabilities.
Work with functional leaders to identify capability gaps, resolve constraints, improve onboarding, and align internal and external capacity with strategic priorities.

Risk, Compliance, and Delivery Assurance

Establish portfolio-level approaches to risk, issue, dependency, assumption, and decision management, ensuring material concerns are identified early, escalated appropriately, and managed through resolution.
Provide oversight of scope, schedule, cost, quality, benefits, adoption, operational readiness, and delivery performance across the portfolio.
Ensure portfolio activities and external arrangements comply with relevant pharmaceutical and technology requirements, including data governance, GDPR and privacy, information security, intellectual property, procurement, ethical, quality, and regulatory frameworks.
Anticipate and manage delivery underperformance, supplier failure, commercial disputes, IP complexity, changing priorities, financial pressure, data and technology dependencies, and regulatory constraints.

Stakeholder Engagement and Change Enablement

Build trusted relationships with AISI and Enterprise AI leaders, therapeutic and scientific areas, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Legal, HR, Operations, and external partners.
Facilitate alignment on priorities, investment choices, delivery expectations, trade-offs, and accountabilities across a global matrix organization.
Communicate complex portfolio, financial, commercial, and delivery matters clearly to senior leaders and diverse stakeholder groups.
Champion adoption of portfolio standards, transparent governance, and collaborative delivery while preserving the speed and experimentation required for AI innovation.

Leadership

Lead and develop high-performing portfolio management, governance, and business-operations capabilities, directly and through matrix teams and managed-service providers.
Create a culture of accountability, collaboration, customer focus, continuous improvement, reuse, and measurable value delivery.
Set clear standards and build scalable capabilities from the ground up, enabling consistent ways of working across functions and geographies.
Contribute to AISI functional strategy and operating model evolution as the organization, technology landscape, and partnership ecosystem mature.

Essential

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree in business, technology, finance, life sciences, project management, law, data science, or a related discipline; a Master's degree or equivalent extensive professional experience is preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience across portfolio management, program or project management, business operations, financial management, alliance or partnership management, supplier governance, contracting, or a related discipline in a complex global organization.
Demonstrated experience leading portfolio management and process-transformation initiatives, including demand intake, value-based prioritization, governance, investment planning, resource allocation, delivery assurance, and benefits realization.
Strong financial acumen, including business-case development, long-term planning, investment tracking, forecasting, budget management, accruals, variance analysis, cross-charges, purchase orders, and resource recharges.
Experience managing suppliers, strategic partners, external collaborations, or managed services, including contracts, service levels, performance, commercial risk, value for money, and issue resolution.
Experience designing and implementing operating models, decision rights, governance forums, processes, RACI frameworks, dashboards, and management information.
Proven success influencing senior leaders and delivering through cross-functional teams, matrix structures, third parties, and managed-service providers.
Ability to operate with limited direction in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and make sound decisions that balance scientific and strategic value, risk, cost, capacity, compliance, and delivery feasibility.
Exceptional written, verbal, influencing, relationship management, and organizational skills.

Desirable

Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, life sciences, or another highly regulated technology environment.
Working knowledge of AI and machine-learning ecosystems, data partnerships, cloud platforms, digital products, technology platforms, and platform-based delivery models.
Understanding of pharmaceutical research and development and how AI, data, platforms, and external partnerships create scientific and competitive advantage.
Experience establishing or scaling portfolio management, alliance management, PMO, or business-operations function.
Experience with Agile, Scrum, SAFe, Lean Portfolio Management, Waterfall, Design Thinking, or hybrid delivery approaches.
Experience with ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, and comparable portfolio, project, financial, procurement, or service-management tools.
Knowledge of data governance, privacy, information security, intellectual property, quality, regulatory compliance, and IT risk management.
Professional qualifications such as PMP, PRINCE2, MSP, Scrum, SAFe, or equivalent portfolio, program, commercial, or supplier-management credentials.

Leadership Capabilities

Strategic thinking: Connects scientific and enterprise strategy to investment choices, delivery priorities, and measurable value.
Enterprise perspective: Optimizes across the portfolio, promotes reuse and scalability, and avoids isolated solutions.
Execution discipline: Establishes clear governance and follows through to achieve reliable delivery and benefits realization.

Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

The Role

As Director, Valuations, you will lead the oversight of day-to-day valuation activities, including the development of valuation models, implementation of key controls, and delivery of insightful portfolio-level reporting.

Working closely with global investment teams and key stakeholders, you will manage the valuation of private investments across multiple asset classes (with a focus on Infrastructure and Sustainable Energies investments), providinge guidance on complex valuations, enhancinge valuation practices, and delivering analysis to support informed decision-making. You will also lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

The Team

CPP Investments' Finance department plays a critical role in supporting the integrity of the Fund's financial reporting and investment valuations, providing independent oversight of valuation processes, controls, and results across a globally diversified investment portfolio.

Within Finance, the Valuations team brings specialized expertise in assessing the fair value of complex investments through rigorous valuation methodologies, financial modelling, and independent judgment. Working closely with global investment teams, external valuation specialists, and governance stakeholders, the team strengthens valuation practices, delivers portfolio insights, and supports transparent, consistent, and well-governed investment valuations.

Accountabilities

Lead the planning and execution of private investment valuations, identifying material valuation movements and delivering insightful analysis across the portfolio, with a focus on Infrastructure and Sustainable Energies.
Partner with global investment teams and cross-functional stakeholders on valuation activities, including the onboarding of new investments, while fostering strong relationships and sharing valuation expertise across the Fund.
Oversee external valuation specialists, services, and relationships, ensuring effective controls, rigorous methodologies, and consistent valuation practices.
Direct the preparation and review of valuation reports and portfolio-level insights for investment teams, the Valuation Committee, Audit Committee, and other Board-level stakeholders.
Provide guidance on complex financial models, critically assessing key assumptions, valuation sensitivities, and risks to support sound decision-making.
Drive enhancements to valuation methodologies, policies, reporting, and processes, including the adoption of AI and emerging technologies to improve efficiency, scalability, and insights.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team through recruitment, mentorship, regular feedback, and professional development, fostering collaboration and accountability.

What You Bring

8+ years of relevant experience in professional valuation services, pension funds, private equity, and/or investment banking.
An undergraduate degree or college diploma in a related field, such as Business or Economics; a relevant professional designation is considered an asset.
Advanced knowledge of valuation standards and methodologies, with strong financial modelling, research, and analytical capabilities.
Sound professional judgment, with the ability to assess complex financial models, challenge assumptions, evaluate sensitivities, and identify key risks.
Experience leading complex projects, improving processes, and collaborating effectively with investment teams, cross-functional partners, and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to lead inclusively, mentor and develop professionals, and communicate complex valuation insights clearly to senior stakeholders.
Strong relationship management and communication skills; advanced experience with Tableau, VBA, Python, or SQL is considered an asset.

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

jobs.title: Program Director, Risk Transformation & Execution
jobs.description:
This position is accountable for leading global risk transformation and execution initiatives for Global Operations Risk and Controls, with primary responsibility for the Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) program across Line 1. The role will translate strategy into practical execution plans, coordinate delivery across businesses and functions, and provide senior leaders with clear visibility into progress, quality, risk, and outcomes.

The role combines enterprise program leadership, data analytics, executive reporting, and identification of AI and automation opportunities. The successful candidate will work directly with complex and imperfect data, conduct targeted quality reviews, challenge scope and assumptions, identify trends and themes, and translate findings into practical recommendations. As priorities evolve, the role will apply these capabilities to other Operations Risk and Control Transformation initiatives.

This is a highly visible individual-contributor role requiring strong judgment, analytical capability, and the ability to lead across a complex global organization through influence rather than formal authority.

Position Responsibilities

Lead global risk transformation and execution

Own integrated plans, milestones, governance, and escalation for global risk transformation initiatives, with RCSA as the initial priority.
Drive delivery across businesses and functions, challenging scope, capacity, sequencing, and other risks to committed outcomes.
Build alignment and accountability across ELT areas, L1B teams, Process Owners, Line 2, Technology, and delivery partners through influence rather than formal authority.

Generate actionable insights

Analyze risk, control, execution, and remediation data to identify trends, gaps, emerging risks, and management actions.
Conduct targeted business analysis and sample quality reviews, including assessments of scope, exceptions, control effectiveness, and supporting evidence.
Translate findings into clear requirements, practical recommendations, and targeted feedback for accountable teams.

Enable senior leadership decisions

Deliver concise ELT and ERC reporting on execution, delivery confidence, control effectiveness, quality, and emerging risks.
Create clear executive narratives that explain what is progressing well, what requires attention, why it matters, and what action is needed.
Present credible options and recommendations where leadership decisions on scope, timing, capacity, prioritization, or investment are required.

Advance AI, automation, and process improvement

Effectively use AI tools to improve manual processes, deepen insights, and drive efficiency.
Identify high-value opportunities for automation, analytics, and process redesign.
Define and prioritize practical use cases, then engage the broader team and delivery partners to design and implement solutions.
Support adoption and measure whether new capabilities improve execution speed, quality, consistency, and risk outcomes.

Qualifications

Significant experience in operational risk, controls, transformation, program management, data analytics, or a related financial-services discipline.
Demonstrated experience leading or supporting RCSA execution, control assessment and testing, or a comparable enterprise risk program is required.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies.

jobs.title: Director, Product Design
jobs.description:
At Replicant, we believe AI should work for people, starting with customer service. That's why we built a platform that helps contact centers resolve more requests, proactively identify issues, and improve agent performance with AI-powered conversation intelligence and AI agents that act like your best reps.

Our AI agents handle millions of calls every month for Fortune 500 companies and high-growth innovators. From processing payments to booking appointments and authenticating users, they help customers get what they need instantly, 24/7. Meanwhile, our real-time conversation insights help contact center leaders coach better and improve every interaction.

We're leading the shift from legacy systems to AI-first service, powered by large language models (LLMs) and designed for enterprise scale, security, and empathy. If you're excited by the potential of LLMs, voice AI, and building category-defining technology with a kind, ambitious team, you'll love it here.

About The Role

This role reports to the VP of Product, owns the practice outright, and comes with two designers attached – our Conversation Design Lead and a Lead / Principal Product Designer whose role you’ll define and hire.

Roughly 80% of your time goes into the work itself, and we mean owning high-leverage product design decisions rather than delivering via management of a team. You’ll be accountable for product design decisions and direction across every surface — the sales conversation, the deployments our delivery team configures, the AI agent talking to a customer, the analytics an operator reads every morning.

The other 20% is designing and running the product design practice to increase design’s leverage across the organization. We’re looking to you to help us get design right – we’ve tried to build design here twice and we’ve under-resourced it both times. Our org has grown up as sales- and engineering-led, and in this role you’ll shepherd how we grow and mature through product and design leadership. As the design practice grows into a pillar of our product function, this role grows with it.

If you want a green field to help demonstrate how powerful a force product design can be – and you want to do that while applying cutting-edge HCI to age-old problems of providing better customer service – this is the role for you.

What You'll Do

Own the whole customer experience, interface included. A customer's experience of Replicant runs from the sales conversation, through a deployment our delivery team configures, into an AI agent that talks to their customers, and back out through the analytics their operators read daily.
Set the information architecture for a converging platform. Our conversation intelligence and agent-building products grew separately and are now becoming one product. You decide what the objects are, what they're called, and how someone moves between them.
Own the design system's architecture and the rules around it. The foundation exists — components in Figma and in Storybook. What's missing is a pattern language, documented decisions about when to use what, and a contribution model engineers can build against. You set that architecture, govern it, and are accountable for it existing.
Extend design's influence past the work you do yourself. Much of the customer-facing experience here gets shaped by people outside your team: product managers, delivery engineers who configure agents, solutions engineers in demos. Raising the bar means influencing them, giving them something good enough to follow, and telling them no when it matters.
Drive rapid prototype-and-validation loops. You'll talk to internal customers, contact center operators and turn what you hear into design decisions, owning method as well as findings. You’ll create and drive a best-in-class prototype-and-validate loop.
Bring product design and conversation design together. Our product is a conversation, so we've put both disciplines in one practice. You own how they come together and the research practice underneath both.

What You'll Bring

You think in systems and journeys. Before asking which control a step needs, you ask whether the step needs to exist. You've designed across touchpoints that weren't all interfaces: a call, a handoff, an email, a conversation with a human agent.
You have a real HCI or interaction-design foundation. You can reason from first principles about how people perceive, learn, form expectations, and recover from error, rather than from patterns you've seen in other products. Voice, conversational, and graphical interfaces all sit inside our product, and we need someone who can move between them without starting over each time.
You've driven change through resistance. You've moved an entrenched team over months, not just changed one executive's mind in one meeting. You can describe what you were up against and what it took.
You lead with the human and you integrate business outcomes and thinking without being asked. You've spent time close to the PM role, or worked with product closely enough that you think that way anyway. You can point to specific decisions that changed because of a conversation you personally had with a customer.
You've governed a design system, not only built one. Contribution, documentation, deprecation, and the arguments that come with them. You can describe a time you told someone no and why. The governance matters more to us than how many components you drew.
You find the problems and set your own priorities. You identify opportunities the team hadn't seen and make the case for them. You converge without being pushed and escalate the right things at the right time.
You're AI-native in your practice. You use these tools in real design work and have earned opinions about where they help and where they degrade quality. You've built workflows or assets other people adopted.
You lead people and hold a room. Setting direction, giving hard feedback, running a critique, growing someone's craft, and hiring. You can also hold your position in front of executives and customers. Formal management experience helps; evidence that designers got better working with you matters more than a title.

Requirements

Based in a US or Canadian timezone
10+ years of product design experience, including 2-3+ at the director or principal level
Experience leading or growing designers, whether or not you had the title
Experience owning design for an enterprise or operational product

We care about the scope of what you've owned, not years on a résumé. If you're unsure whether you're at this level, apply anyway. We'd rather assess it than have you self-select out.

NICE TO HAVE

Figma fluency on the system side: components, variants, libraries, variables, tokens. Enough to hold your hire to a standard and to work in the files yourself.
Comfort moving between Figma and code (Storybook, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, or tools like Cursor and Claude Code). If you want to pick up UI-level changes yourself, that's open to you with preview environments and engineering review.
Experience designing AI or conversational products, especially where the output was non-deterministic and you had to design failure states, trust, correction, and recovery.
Experience with operational or contact center tooling.
Experience defining a design practice from close to nothing.
Experience leading designers across more than one discipline — product, conversation, content, or research.

For All Full-time Employees, We Offer

🌴 In-person connection that counts
: company-wide offsites and smaller team gatherings designed to make remote work feel personal

🖥️ Tech & learning stipend
: Conferences, books, courses — interested? We’ll fund them

📍 Remote by design
: We’re distributed — no guilt about life events, we trust you to manage your calendar

🏋️ Health & wellness
: Flexible vacations, paid sabbatical after 5 years, comprehensive benefits, plus a stipend to support your physical and mental well-being

💸 Compensation that matches your impact
: competitive salaries in the company you’re helping to build

📈 Equity with upside
: We believe in shared ownership—You’ll own a real piece of a fast-growing AI company

Our Values

Replicant has three core values. It is critical that everyone who joins the team feels excited and moved by these values as every new team member makes an impact on our culture.

Blade Runners:
We take ownership and pride to influence the outcomes of our goals. We are successful, and like a Blade Runner, use the tools at our disposal to reach our objectives. We value open and honest communication and proactively seek feedback along the way. We are a company driven to grow and achieve both individually and as a team.

Bread Makers:
We are humble and strive toward an egalitarian culture. No task is too big or too small. We work together to achieve our goals and develop our company mission. We believe that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts in everything that we do.

Självdistans (Self-Distance):
Självdistans is Swedish for self-distance. It's the ability to critically reflect on oneself and one's relations from an external perspective. With this in mind, we act with objectivity and always remember that we are not our work. There's no perfect science to growing a team or business, but we trust everyone at Replicant to point out our blind spots and humbly admit their own.

Replicant is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at talent@replicant.ai and we’ll work to meet your needs.

Who we are

At WELLSTAR, we are committed to reshaping Canadian healthcare by leveraging technology to address the administrative burdens that pull physicians away from their true calling—patient care. Our mission is to support providers and patients, shifting the emphasis back to quality, timeliness, and positive outcomes. With a comprehensive suite of technology solutions, we have successfully helped thousands of providers adopt and benefit from modern, interoperable technologies that improve patient outcomes and system efficiency.

Whether you are in research and development, administration, communications, operations leadership, or technology, joining us now is an opportunity to play a critical role in transforming how healthcare is managed and experienced in Canada.

The opportunity

WELLSTAR, a majority-owned subsidiary of WELL Health Technologies Corp, is a high-growth SaaS company with a focused objective of reshaping healthcare through digital enablement. Our innovative solutions are designed to streamline care delivery, integrate healthcare systems and improve patient outcomes.

Reporting to the VP, Product Management, we are hiring a Director, UI/UX Design to lead the design function for the Clinical Platform Group. As our new Director, UI/UX Design, you will lead and develop an established team of designers while owning the quality, consistency, and evolution of the end-to-end product experience. You will set the design direction for a modern, AI-first EMR platform, strengthen user research and design practices, and ensure the needs of clinicians remain central to how the product evolves. Working as a peer to Product and Engineering leadership, you will bring greater structure and consistency to how teams collaborate from problem definition and discovery through design, development, and release.

This is a remote-first role open to candidates anywhere in Canada, with occasional travel for team on-sites and clinic visits.

What’s in it for you

Leadership and influence. You will step into an established design team with the opportunity to make a strong team even better. You will have the scope to develop designers, raise the bar on craft and consistency, and shape how the design function evolves as the product and organization grow. Working alongside Product and Engineering leadership, you will have a voice in decisions that influence both the product experience and how teams work together.

Shape an AI-first healthcare experience. You will help define how clinicians interact with AI in a product they rely on to deliver care. From how AI-generated suggestions are presented to how confidence, transparency, and clinician control are built into the experience, you will influence some of the most important design questions facing Nexus AI™ EMR as the platform evolves.

Build better ways of working. You will have the opportunity to strengthen and mature an existing design practice rather than build one from the ground up. You will refine research, design processes, cross-functional collaboration, and the design system, creating the structure that helps designers do their best work and enables Product, Design, and Engineering to move forward together.

What you will do:

Lead and develop the design team.
You will coach and support an established team of designers, creating clear ownership, providing meaningful feedback, and helping each person build on their strengths and grow. You will foster a collaborative critique culture and create the conditions for the team to consistently deliver high-quality work.
Own the end-to-end product experience.
You will be accountable for the quality, consistency, and coherence of the Clinical Platform Group product experience across clinical and administrative workflows. You will establish and uphold a high design standard, incorporating accessibility and clinical safety considerations into how experiences are designed and delivered.
Shape AI-assisted experiences.
You will set the design direction for how AI is integrated into clinical workflows, including how suggestions are surfaced, confidence and provenance are communicated, and clinicians remain in control. You will help ensure AI-enabled experiences are practical, intuitive, and designed around the realities of clinical care.
Strengthen how Design, Product, and Engineering work together.
You will partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to bring design into problem definition, discovery, refinement, and delivery. You will improve handoffs and feedback loops so requirements, designs, edge cases, and intended experiences are clearly understood and carried through to what is released.
Evolve design practices and systems.
You will refine the design process from intake and discovery through critique, handoff, and design QA, keeping it structured without creating unnecessary complexity. You will champion the design system, patterns, documentation, and tools that help the team work efficiently and deliver a consistent experience.
Bring users closer to product decisions.
You will establish a sustainable approach to user research, including interviews and engagement with clinics, and ensure insights are shared effectively across Design, Product, and Engineering. You will help turn what the team learns from clinicians and customers into meaningful improvements to the product and roadmap.

What you bring:

The design leadership experience.
You have experience leading and developing product designers, including coaching, providing meaningful feedback, supporting career development, and managing performance. You know how to assess the strengths of an established team, build trust, and create the clarity and support people need to do their best work.
The product design expertise.
You have designed and shipped complex, workflow-heavy software where usability, accuracy, and attention to detail matter. You bring strong design judgment and can critically evaluate work, challenge assumptions, and raise the quality and consistency of the user experience without imposing a rigid design philosophy.
The ability to evolve a design practice.
You have improved how a design team operates, whether through stronger discovery and research practices, critique and review, design systems, handoffs, or design QA. You can introduce structure without unnecessary process and understand how to measure whether changes are making the team and the product better.
The cross-functional approach.
You have worked closely with Product and Engineering teams in an agile product environment and understand how design fits into discovery, backlog refinement, sprint planning, development, and release. You can influence peers and senior stakeholders, communicate design decisions and trade-offs clearly, and build alignment around the user experience.
The curiosity for AI-enabled design.
You are comfortable exploring AI-assisted design tools and bring a thoughtful perspective on where they can improve speed and effectiveness without compromising craft or consistency. Experience designing AI or LLM-powered products, including human-in-the-loop experiences, would be an asset.
The adaptability.
You design for the needs of the people using the product rather than following a single definition of what good UX should look like. You can work with complex, information-dense experiences and balance user needs, accessibility, technical constraints, and the realities of the environment in which the product is used. Experience in healthcare, EMR/EHR products, or another regulated environment is an asset.

Why join us?

WELLSTAR is a leading healthcare technology company dedicated to reshaping healthcare through digital enablement. We provide a comprehensive, holistic solution for healthcare providers across Canada, with over 40% of practitioners currently using our products and services.

What you can expect from our interview process:

A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
A virtual interview with the VP, Product Management focused on your design leadership experience, approach to developing and supporting a design team, and experience strengthening collaboration across Design, Product, and Engineering.
A final interview with the team focused on team dynamics, collaboration and how you would contribute to the broader team.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is $120-150K. The salary will be determined based on several factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and the needs of the organization. At WELLSTAR, we are committed to fair and equitable compensation and aim to provide a competitive salary that reflects the value and expertise of the successful candidate.

Apply now.

Interested in applying but worried you don't have it all? At WELLSTAR, we know not everyone gains their experience following a traditional path. If you share our values, want to make a difference in healthcare technology solutions, and meet 70% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Express your interest here.

About Solen Software Group

Solen Software Group is an evergreen holding company that acquires and operates proven software businesses that have significant growth potential in a variety of vertical markets, enabling them to be market leaders in their niche industry. About The Role

The Director of FP&A will own how Solen plans, forecasts, measures, and makes decisions across our portfolio of 20+ software companies and the holding company. Reporting to the CFO, this role partners as a peer with the Controller: the Controller owns the close, books, and consolidated actuals, while the Director of FP&A owns the budget, forecast, KPIs, Monthly Business Review, and the models behind capital allocation and acquisitions.

This is a build-as-you-go role. Our businesses run with real autonomy and span recurring SaaS, usage-based fees, professional services, and hardware. You will design the planning and reporting engine that replaces today's manual, company-by-company reporting, build the team that runs it, and support the CFO in raising debt and equity capital.

This is a highly strategic, hands-on leadership role working directly with the CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and General Managers of our operating companies (OpCos).

Key Responsibilities

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Own the annual budget, quarterly re-forecast, rolling forecast, and long-range plan across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with one planning calendar and standard templates.
Build driver-based models suited to each revenue model: ARR, retention and churn cohorts, usage volumes, utilization and billable hours, hardware and license sales, and headcount.
Produce a consolidated, scenario-ready outlook for the CFO, CEO, and board.
Own forward cash forecasting and liquidity and covenant-headroom modelling in partnership with the Controller.
Track forecast accuracy, explain material misses, and continuously improve the process.

Portfolio Performance & KPIs

Define and deploy a consistent KPI framework across the portfolio, benchmarked against Solen's investment thesis.
Track unit economics, retention cohorts, customer profitability, and cost structure by function to benchmark OpCos against each other and best-in-class.
Support OpCo leaders on pricing, customer profitability, cost optimization, and financial turnarounds.

Monthly Business Review & Reporting

Own the MBR cadence, structure, KPI package, and follow-through on action items, raising the quality of insight in every review.
Partner with divisional controllers who run OpCo-level MBRs, equipping them with better data, tools, and insight.
Standardize and automate management reporting and dashboards in Power BI, and develop digital, real-time, and AI-native reporting.
Own the reporting roadmap, defining every metric once and building core reports such as the ARR bridge, budget-versus-actual, organic versus inorganic growth, EBITDA bridge, free cash flow, 13-week cash forecast, and return on invested capital.

Capital Allocation, Capital Raising & M&A

Build the models that guide capital allocation across reinvestment, bolt-on acquisitions, and cash returned to the HoldCo.
Support the CFO and deal team with acquisition models: valuation, diligence, pro formas, and synergy cases.
Support the CFO on debt and equity raises and refinancing with models, projections, scenario analysis, and lender and investor materials.
Track post-acquisition performance against the underwriting case and onboard new acquisitions into planning and KPIs from day one.

FP&A Team Build-Out

Design the FP&A operating model for a lean, decentralized portfolio.
Recruit, hire, and develop a best-in-class FP&A and business partner team.
Establish clear ownership between FP&A, the Controller, divisional controllers, and OpCo finance leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, candor, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field; MBA or CFA preferred.
8+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience.
Direct ownership of budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning for a multi-entity or decentralized business (e.g., PE-backed platform, roll-up, or multi-brand company).
Experience building, leading, and developing an FP&A or business partner team.
Excellent financial modelling skills, including driver-based forecasting and scenario analysis; advanced Excel.
Experience designing KPI frameworks and running recurring business reviews with operating leaders.
Experience building management reporting and dashboards in a BI tool.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for a CEO, board, or non-finance operator.
Willing to work on-site in Salt Lake City or Park City, UT, or in New York, NY with regular travel to Utah, and occasional international travel to Lisbon, Portugal.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in B2B or vertical market SaaS, including ARR, GRR/NRR, and cohort analysis.
Experience modelling mixed revenue streams: subscription, usage-based, professional services, and hardware.
Background in private equity, permanent capital, investment banking, or Big-4 transaction advisory.
Experience supporting debt or equity raises or refinancing.
Experience using AI tools to automate manual finance work.
Working knowledge of Power BI and Sage Intacct or a comparable multi-entity ERP.
Experience with multi-currency planning and teams based outside the U.S.

What Success Looks Like

A consistent KPI framework is adopted by every OpCo, with each company viewed on one comparable scorecard against Solen's investment thesis.
The MBR runs on a predictable cadence with a standardized, automated package, and the highest-priority reports are live.

Capital allocation, acquisition, and financing models exist and have informed real decisions.
The CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and GMs seek FP&A's view before major decisions.

Solen-isms (How We Operate)

Ownership Mindset: We own the mission. We don't wait to be told. We lead, fix, and build as if it were ours. When problems arise, we run toward them, not away.
Benchmark to Best: We seek out excellence. We measure ourselves against the best and adapt quickly, always looking for the edge that moves us forward.

Disagree & Commit: Leaders disagree openly and constructively, regardless of title or tenure, because truth is how we avoid bureaucracy and benchmark to best.
Figureitoutiveness: Embracing challenges, fostering growth, and taking initiative, leaders thrive on hard work and high failure tolerance.
Mutual Elevation: Committed to growth, elevating teams, developing future leaders, and removing barriers to mastery and joy.

Will to Win: Leaders relentlessly pursue potential, reject mediocrity, and get what they tolerate.
Dialectical: We learn through conversation. We ask, listen, question, and evolve — valuing disagreement as a tool for alignment and deeper understanding.
Frugality: Achieving more with less, focusing on quality, long-term value, and company-wide responsibility.
Candor: We communicate with integrity, transparency, and respect in all conversations.
Kaizen: Kaizen is continuous improvement as a way of life. Leaders make hundreds of small upgrades that compound, turning lessons into standards and standards into durable systems.

What You Will Do

You will strengthen the team’s crisis-management role, ensuring that the CMF is not simply a framework on paper but a practical, tested and trusted operating model for timely assessment, escalation, executive decision-making and coordinated response.

The risk landscape is changing quickly. You will position CMCO to address faster-moving cyber, technology, third-party, physical and operational disruptions. You will support a multi-year effort to help the Bank anticipate AI-enabled threats, maintain critical operations during technology disruption, and strengthen the way business, technology, cyber, risk and suppliers work together on resilience.

You will lead CMCO’s evolution from a primarily planning-based function to an active, business-focused and AI-enabled resilience capability. The emphasis will be on the processes and operations that matter most, the dependencies that support them, practical contingency measures, scenario-based testing, and clear evidence that the Bank can continue priority outcomes under severe but plausible conditions.

In addition, you will

Lead and strengthen the Crisis Management Framework. Own the ongoing development, operationalization and assurance of the CMF, including governance, roles, escalation pathways, activation criteria, decision support, communications, playbooks and links to departmental and specialist incident-response arrangements.
Build a stronger crisis-management capability. Develop the team’s ability to assess emerging incidents, convene the right expertise quickly, maintain situational awareness, support executives, coordinate the corporate response and drive disciplined follow-through.
Adapt to the current risk environment. Translate emerging AI and cyber risks into practical business-readiness actions: confirm which critical operations must continue, understand technology and third-party dependencies, prepare for degraded service or accelerated remediation, and ensure contingency and recovery approaches are realistic.
Focus effort where it matters most. Use criticality, disruption tolerance, risk, dependency exposure and evidence to prioritize the processes requiring deeper assessment and investment. Simplify requirements and reduce low-value process, documentation and reporting.
Direct scenario-based testing. Establish a coordinated exercise program using severe but plausible scenarios, including cyber disruption, technology outages, third-party failures, loss of facilities, people constraints and multiple concurrent incidents. Test decision rights, escalation, workarounds, communications, recovery sequencing and executive readiness.
Lead the business-partner model. Set direction for CMCO business partners who advise departments, challenge and validate preparedness, connect dependencies across the enterprise and convert findings into practical, owned and measurable improvements.

new_jobs.title: Director, Product Design
new_jobs.description:
At Replicant, we believe AI should work for people, starting with customer service. That's why we built a platform that helps contact centers resolve more requests, proactively identify issues, and improve agent performance with AI-powered conversation intelligence and AI agents that act like your best reps.

Our AI agents handle millions of calls every month for Fortune 500 companies and high-growth innovators. From processing payments to booking appointments and authenticating users, they help customers get what they need instantly, 24/7. Meanwhile, our real-time conversation insights help contact center leaders coach better and improve every interaction.

We're leading the shift from legacy systems to AI-first service, powered by large language models (LLMs) and designed for enterprise scale, security, and empathy. If you're excited by the potential of LLMs, voice AI, and building category-defining technology with a kind, ambitious team, you'll love it here.

About The Role

This role reports to the VP of Product, owns the practice outright, and comes with two designers attached – our Conversation Design Lead and a Lead / Principal Product Designer whose role you’ll define and hire.

Roughly 80% of your time goes into the work itself, and we mean owning high-leverage product design decisions rather than delivering via management of a team. You’ll be accountable for product design decisions and direction across every surface — the sales conversation, the deployments our delivery team configures, the AI agent talking to a customer, the analytics an operator reads every morning.

The other 20% is designing and running the product design practice to increase design’s leverage across the organization. We’re looking to you to help us get design right – we’ve tried to build design here twice and we’ve under-resourced it both times. Our org has grown up as sales- and engineering-led, and in this role you’ll shepherd how we grow and mature through product and design leadership. As the design practice grows into a pillar of our product function, this role grows with it.

If you want a green field to help demonstrate how powerful a force product design can be – and you want to do that while applying cutting-edge HCI to age-old problems of providing better customer service – this is the role for you.

What You'll Do

Own the whole customer experience, interface included. A customer's experience of Replicant runs from the sales conversation, through a deployment our delivery team configures, into an AI agent that talks to their customers, and back out through the analytics their operators read daily.
Set the information architecture for a converging platform. Our conversation intelligence and agent-building products grew separately and are now becoming one product. You decide what the objects are, what they're called, and how someone moves between them.
Own the design system's architecture and the rules around it. The foundation exists — components in Figma and in Storybook. What's missing is a pattern language, documented decisions about when to use what, and a contribution model engineers can build against. You set that architecture, govern it, and are accountable for it existing.
Extend design's influence past the work you do yourself. Much of the customer-facing experience here gets shaped by people outside your team: product managers, delivery engineers who configure agents, solutions engineers in demos. Raising the bar means influencing them, giving them something good enough to follow, and telling them no when it matters.
Drive rapid prototype-and-validation loops. You'll talk to internal customers, contact center operators and turn what you hear into design decisions, owning method as well as findings. You’ll create and drive a best-in-class prototype-and-validate loop.
Bring product design and conversation design together. Our product is a conversation, so we've put both disciplines in one practice. You own how they come together and the research practice underneath both.

What You'll Bring

You think in systems and journeys. Before asking which control a step needs, you ask whether the step needs to exist. You've designed across touchpoints that weren't all interfaces: a call, a handoff, an email, a conversation with a human agent.
You have a real HCI or interaction-design foundation. You can reason from first principles about how people perceive, learn, form expectations, and recover from error, rather than from patterns you've seen in other products. Voice, conversational, and graphical interfaces all sit inside our product, and we need someone who can move between them without starting over each time.
You've driven change through resistance. You've moved an entrenched team over months, not just changed one executive's mind in one meeting. You can describe what you were up against and what it took.
You lead with the human and you integrate business outcomes and thinking without being asked. You've spent time close to the PM role, or worked with product closely enough that you think that way anyway. You can point to specific decisions that changed because of a conversation you personally had with a customer.
You've governed a design system, not only built one. Contribution, documentation, deprecation, and the arguments that come with them. You can describe a time you told someone no and why. The governance matters more to us than how many components you drew.
You find the problems and set your own priorities. You identify opportunities the team hadn't seen and make the case for them. You converge without being pushed and escalate the right things at the right time.
You're AI-native in your practice. You use these tools in real design work and have earned opinions about where they help and where they degrade quality. You've built workflows or assets other people adopted.
You lead people and hold a room. Setting direction, giving hard feedback, running a critique, growing someone's craft, and hiring. You can also hold your position in front of executives and customers. Formal management experience helps; evidence that designers got better working with you matters more than a title.

Requirements

Based in a US or Canadian timezone
10+ years of product design experience, including 2-3+ at the director or principal level
Experience leading or growing designers, whether or not you had the title
Experience owning design for an enterprise or operational product

We care about the scope of what you've owned, not years on a résumé. If you're unsure whether you're at this level, apply anyway. We'd rather assess it than have you self-select out.

NICE TO HAVE

Figma fluency on the system side: components, variants, libraries, variables, tokens. Enough to hold your hire to a standard and to work in the files yourself.
Comfort moving between Figma and code (Storybook, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, or tools like Cursor and Claude Code). If you want to pick up UI-level changes yourself, that's open to you with preview environments and engineering review.
Experience designing AI or conversational products, especially where the output was non-deterministic and you had to design failure states, trust, correction, and recovery.
Experience with operational or contact center tooling.
Experience defining a design practice from close to nothing.
Experience leading designers across more than one discipline — product, conversation, content, or research.

For All Full-time Employees, We Offer

🌴 In-person connection that counts
: company-wide offsites and smaller team gatherings designed to make remote work feel personal

🖥️ Tech & learning stipend
: Conferences, books, courses — interested? We’ll fund them

📍 Remote by design
: We’re distributed — no guilt about life events, we trust you to manage your calendar

🏋️ Health & wellness
: Flexible vacations, paid sabbatical after 5 years, comprehensive benefits, plus a stipend to support your physical and mental well-being

💸 Compensation that matches your impact
: competitive salaries in the company you’re helping to build

📈 Equity with upside
: We believe in shared ownership—You’ll own a real piece of a fast-growing AI company

Our Values

Replicant has three core values. It is critical that everyone who joins the team feels excited and moved by these values as every new team member makes an impact on our culture.

Blade Runners:
We take ownership and pride to influence the outcomes of our goals. We are successful, and like a Blade Runner, use the tools at our disposal to reach our objectives. We value open and honest communication and proactively seek feedback along the way. We are a company driven to grow and achieve both individually and as a team.

Bread Makers:
We are humble and strive toward an egalitarian culture. No task is too big or too small. We work together to achieve our goals and develop our company mission. We believe that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts in everything that we do.

Självdistans (Self-Distance):
Självdistans is Swedish for self-distance. It's the ability to critically reflect on oneself and one's relations from an external perspective. With this in mind, we act with objectivity and always remember that we are not our work. There's no perfect science to growing a team or business, but we trust everyone at Replicant to point out our blind spots and humbly admit their own.

Replicant is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and equitable workplace that is built on trust, support and respect. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. Accommodation is available upon request at any point during our recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please speak to your talent acquisition partner or email us at talent@replicant.ai and we’ll work to meet your needs.

WELLSTAR, a majority-owned subsidiary of WELL Health Technologies Corp, is a high-growth SaaS company with a focused objective of reshaping healthcare through digital enablement. Our innovative solutions are designed to streamline care delivery, integrate healthcare systems and improve patient outcomes.

Reporting to the VP, Product Management, we are hiring a Director, UI/UX Design to lead the design function for the Clinical Platform Group. As our new Director, UI/UX Design, you will lead and develop an established team of designers while owning the quality, consistency, and evolution of the end-to-end product experience. You will set the design direction for a modern, AI-first EMR platform, strengthen user research and design practices, and ensure the needs of clinicians remain central to how the product evolves. Working as a peer to Product and Engineering leadership, you will bring greater structure and consistency to how teams collaborate from problem definition and discovery through design, development, and release.

This is a remote-first role open to candidates anywhere in Canada, with occasional travel for team on-sites and clinic visits.

What’s in it for you

Leadership and influence. You will step into an established design team with the opportunity to make a strong team even better. You will have the scope to develop designers, raise the bar on craft and consistency, and shape how the design function evolves as the product and organization grow. Working alongside Product and Engineering leadership, you will have a voice in decisions that influence both the product experience and how teams work together.

Shape an AI-first healthcare experience. You will help define how clinicians interact with AI in a product they rely on to deliver care. From how AI-generated suggestions are presented to how confidence, transparency, and clinician control are built into the experience, you will influence some of the most important design questions facing Nexus AI™ EMR as the platform evolves.

Build better ways of working. You will have the opportunity to strengthen and mature an existing design practice rather than build one from the ground up. You will refine research, design processes, cross-functional collaboration, and the design system, creating the structure that helps designers do their best work and enables Product, Design, and Engineering to move forward together.

What you will do:

Lead and develop the design team.
You will coach and support an established team of designers, creating clear ownership, providing meaningful feedback, and helping each person build on their strengths and grow. You will foster a collaborative critique culture and create the conditions for the team to consistently deliver high-quality work.
Own the end-to-end product experience.
You will be accountable for the quality, consistency, and coherence of the Clinical Platform Group product experience across clinical and administrative workflows. You will establish and uphold a high design standard, incorporating accessibility and clinical safety considerations into how experiences are designed and delivered.
Shape AI-assisted experiences.
You will set the design direction for how AI is integrated into clinical workflows, including how suggestions are surfaced, confidence and provenance are communicated, and clinicians remain in control. You will help ensure AI-enabled experiences are practical, intuitive, and designed around the realities of clinical care.
Strengthen how Design, Product, and Engineering work together.
You will partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to bring design into problem definition, discovery, refinement, and delivery. You will improve handoffs and feedback loops so requirements, designs, edge cases, and intended experiences are clearly understood and carried through to what is released.
Evolve design practices and systems.
You will refine the design process from intake and discovery through critique, handoff, and design QA, keeping it structured without creating unnecessary complexity. You will champion the design system, patterns, documentation, and tools that help the team work efficiently and deliver a consistent experience.
Bring users closer to product decisions.
You will establish a sustainable approach to user research, including interviews and engagement with clinics, and ensure insights are shared effectively across Design, Product, and Engineering. You will help turn what the team learns from clinicians and customers into meaningful improvements to the product and roadmap.

What you bring:

The design leadership experience.
You have experience leading and developing product designers, including coaching, providing meaningful feedback, supporting career development, and managing performance. You know how to assess the strengths of an established team, build trust, and create the clarity and support people need to do their best work.
The product design expertise.
You have designed and shipped complex, workflow-heavy software where usability, accuracy, and attention to detail matter. You bring strong design judgment and can critically evaluate work, challenge assumptions, and raise the quality and consistency of the user experience without imposing a rigid design philosophy.
The ability to evolve a design practice.
You have improved how a design team operates, whether through stronger discovery and research practices, critique and review, design systems, handoffs, or design QA. The cross-functional approach.
You have worked closely with Product and Engineering teams in an agile product environment and understand how design fits into discovery, backlog refinement, sprint planning, development, and release. You can influence peers and senior stakeholders, communicate design decisions and trade-offs clearly, and build alignment around the user experience.

The adaptability.
You design for the needs of the people using the product rather than following a single definition of what good UX should look like. Experience in healthcare, EMR/EHR products, or another regulated environment is an asset.

About Solen Software Group

Solen Software Group is an evergreen holding company that acquires and operates proven software businesses that have significant growth potential in a variety of vertical markets, enabling them to be market leaders in their niche industry. The Director of FP&A will own how Solen plans, forecasts, measures, and makes decisions across our portfolio of 20+ software companies and the holding company. Reporting to the CFO, this role partners as a peer with the Controller: the Controller owns the close, books, and consolidated actuals, while the Director of FP&A owns the budget, forecast, KPIs, Monthly Business Review, and the models behind capital allocation and acquisitions.

This is a build-as-you-go role. Our businesses run with real autonomy and span recurring SaaS, usage-based fees, professional services, and hardware. You will design the planning and reporting engine that replaces today's manual, company-by-company reporting, build the team that runs it, and support the CFO in raising debt and equity capital.

This is a highly strategic, hands-on leadership role working directly with the CFO, CEO, Portfolio Leaders, and General Managers of our operating companies (OpCos).

Key Responsibilities

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting

Own the annual budget, quarterly re-forecast, rolling forecast, and long-range plan across all OpCos and the HoldCo, with one planning calendar and standard templates.
Build driver-based models suited to each revenue model: ARR, retention and churn cohorts, usage volumes, utilization and billable hours, hardware and license sales, and headcount.
Produce a consolidated, scenario-ready outlook for the CFO, CEO, and board.
Own forward cash forecasting and liquidity and covenant-headroom modelling in partnership with the Controller.
Track forecast accuracy, explain material misses, and continuously improve the process.

Portfolio Performance & KPIs

Define and deploy a consistent KPI framework across the portfolio, benchmarked against Solen's investment thesis.
Track unit economics, retention cohorts, customer profitability, and cost structure by function to benchmark OpCos against each other and best-in-class.
Support OpCo leaders on pricing, customer profitability, cost optimization, and financial turnarounds.

Monthly Business Review & Reporting

Own the MBR cadence, structure, KPI package, and follow-through on action items, raising the quality of insight in every review.
Partner with divisional controllers who run OpCo-level MBRs, equipping them with better data, tools, and insight.
Standardize and automate management reporting and dashboards in Power BI, and develop digital, real-time, and AI-native reporting.
Own the reporting roadmap, defining every metric once and building core reports such as the ARR bridge, budget-versus-actual, organic versus inorganic growth, EBITDA bridge, free cash flow, 13-week cash forecast, and return on invested capital.

Capital Allocation, Capital Raising & M&A

Build the models that guide capital allocation across reinvestment, bolt-on acquisitions, and cash returned to the HoldCo.
Support the CFO and deal team with acquisition models: valuation, diligence, pro formas, and synergy cases.
Support the CFO on debt and equity raises and refinancing with models, projections, scenario analysis, and lender and investor materials.
Track post-acquisition performance against the underwriting case and onboard new acquisitions into planning and KPIs from day one.

FP&A Team Build-Out

Design the FP&A operating model for a lean, decentralized portfolio.
Recruit, hire, and develop a best-in-class FP&A and business partner team.
Establish clear ownership between FP&A, the Controller, divisional controllers, and OpCo finance leaders.
Foster a culture of ownership, candor, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related field; MBA or CFA preferred.
8+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance, or strategic finance experience.
Direct ownership of budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning for a multi-entity or decentralized business (e.g., PE-backed platform, roll-up, or multi-brand company).
Experience building, leading, and developing an FP&A or business partner team.
Excellent financial modelling skills, including driver-based forecasting and scenario analysis; advanced Excel.
Experience designing KPI frameworks and running recurring business reviews with operating leaders.
Experience building management reporting and dashboards in a BI tool.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for a CEO, board, or non-finance operator.
Willing to work on-site in Salt Lake City or Park City, UT, or in New York, NY with regular travel to Utah, and occasional international travel to Lisbon, Portugal.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in B2B or vertical market SaaS, including ARR, GRR/NRR, and cohort analysis.
Experience modelling mixed revenue streams: subscription, usage-based, professional services, and hardware.
Background in private equity, permanent capital, investment banking, or Big-4 transaction advisory.

What Success Looks Like

Ownership Mindset: We own the mission. We don't wait to be told. We lead, fix, and build as if it were ours. When problems arise, we run toward them, not away.
